verdict: REVISE. The reentrant callback fires N+1 times every call with zero diagnostics at N up to 300, no hang. The no-op-repeat case shows real caching (~5x cheaper marginal per-file rate than cold). But the executor's headline claim - that editing one file costs nearly as much as a cold rebuild, so caching is 'largely absent once anything changes' - was an artifact of always editing file index 0, the compilation-order worst case. Independent review, then independently re-confirmed with a durable artifact (editIdx sweep at N=300), showed cost is linear in the number of compilation-order successors after the edited file: editing the last file is statistically indistinguishable from a no-op repeat, editing the first file costs close to cold. The real finding is (c)-with-positional-cost, not (b): FCS incrementally skips the compilation-order prefix before an edit and only re-checks the tail. Caveat that cuts the other way for Myriad specifically: attributed domain types often sit early in build order, which is close to the worst-case position measured.
